findings.title: Auto-merge workflow holds `contents: write` with no environment protection and no head-commit pin
findings.detail: Prior CI-P2-001 persists unchanged at f5cb7c9. dependabot-merge.yml:17-19 declares contents:write + pull-requests:write; :27 runs on the self-hosted lab runner; :46-48 checks `gh pr checks` then runs `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` with no `--match-head-commit`, leaving a TOCTOU window between the check and the merge. No environment protection exists (environments API total_count 0), so the owner-applied `dependabot-approved` label is the only human disposition (BRANCH_PROTECTION.md:95). The workflow is still unexercised (see BP-P3-001), so the failure mode has no observed behavior. Fix: add `--match-head-commit "$(gh pr view ... --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)"`, reduce the token to the minimum scopes the gh calls need, and add an environment with required reviewers when the plan allows (or convert the merge to an owner-run workflow_dispatch). Validation: a fixture asserting the merge command contains --match-head-commit and that no unused write scope is declared.
evidence: .github/workflows/dependabot-merge.yml:46-48 (gh pr checks then gh pr merge, no --match-head-commit)
docs/security/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md:95 (label gate is the human disposition; environment reviewers plan-blocked)

findings.title: external-smoke no longer asserts Cloudflare Access posture and passes on an owner-IP bypass
findings.detail: Still open at f5cb7c9. The header (external-smoke.yml:3-6) and the runs-on comment (:23-25) claim the gate runs from GitHub's network and asserts `302 -> cloudflareaccess.com`, but the job actually runs on [self-hosted, lab] (:26; commit 70292a0b) and check_gated accepts any 302 (:37-42; commit 08e20d1a) as `owner-IP Access bypass; origin reachable`. The latest scheduled run (38067043888, 2026-10-10T16:17Z, runner lab-runner-2) succeeded with exactly that bypass message for iris and soc, while the job summary (:64-67) still says 'must be 302 to cloudflareaccess.com (Access still enforcing)'. An Access regression on iris/soc would not be detected, and the artifact misstates what was verified. Fix: restore an external vantage (DO forwarder/monitor; hosted runners are billing-blocked) or rescope the workflow to origin reachability and record/link where Access posture is verified; correct the header and summary text; make the check a required external check when possible.
evidence: GitHub run 38067043888 job log: 'OK https://iris.mainecybertech.us/ -> 302 (owner-IP Access bypass; origin reachable)' and the same for soc

findings.title: Repository Actions settings default to permissive (write token, PR approvals, any action, no SHA-pin requirement)
findings.detail: Still open at f5cb7c9. Live API: /actions/permissions returns {enabled:true, allowed_actions:'all', sha_pinning_required:false}; /actions/permissions/workflow returns {default_workflow_permissions:'write', can_approve_pull_request_reviews:true}. All three committed workflows declare their own permissions, so the default is latent, not currently exercised: any new workflow without a permissions block gets a read-write token (on a self-hosted runner); Actions may create/approve its own PRs, undermining the review boundary; any marketplace action is allowed; server-side SHA-pin enforcement is off (the repo pins manually and runs zizmor). Fix: set the default workflow permission to `read`; disable 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests'; consider allowed_actions=selected and sha_pinning_required=true. Validation: the API returns read/false; a workflow with no permissions block shows a read-only token in its run log.

findings.title: Hosted-runner fallback is dead; scheduled/queued workflow failures stay silent
findings.detail: Still open, with new live evidence. (a) validate.yml:28 still falls back to `ubuntu-latest` for fork PRs, but GitHub-hosted runners are billing-blocked (external-smoke.yml:26 records this), so fork PRs would get no validation signal; the repo is private, so the path is latent but untested. (b) The dependabot-merge schedule runs of 2026-10-06 (37460608720), 2026-10-07 (37616708114) and 2026-10-08 (37774326519) queued on [self-hosted,linux,x64,lab] with runner_name empty and were cancelled after exactly ~24h - no runner picked them up and nothing alerted; the Oct 9/10 runs succeeded. (c) No workflow contains a notification step (grep of .github/workflows for ntfy/notify/webhook is empty); the CI/CD incident playbook's detection is manual. The weekly validate schedule has run once (37326207794, 2026-10-05, success). Fix: remove/replace the hosted fallback and document the fork-PR policy; add a failure/queue watchdog (e.g., a step posting to the existing ntfy relay, or a Prometheus textfile metric plus alert) for scheduled workflows.
evidence: GitHub runs 37460608720, 37616708114, 37774326519: job queued on [self-hosted,linux,x64,lab], runner_name empty, cancelled after ~24h

findings.title: Three probe workflows remain registered/active with no file on any branch
findings.detail: Still open at f5cb7c9. The Actions API lists 8 workflows; besides the three canonical files and the two dynamic Dependabot workflows, it still lists lab-probe (id 374465077), lab-pwsh-probe (374566273) and testnuc-runner-verify (374995041, path .github/workflows/testnuc-verify.yml), all state=active, while the repository tree contains only validate.yml, external-smoke.yml and dependabot-merge.yml. findings.title: Review package is documented as a CI/release artifact but no CI job builds or publishes it
findings.detail: REPOSITORY.md:51-59 and README.md:118 say the review package is a generated, gitignored delivery artifact 'published as a CI/release artifact' (the HYG-P1-001 rationale that it 'can no longer silently diverge from source'). At f5cb7c9 no workflow references build_review_package.sh, verify_delivery.sh, upload-artifact, id-token or attestations (grep of .github is empty); the GitHub API shows 0 workflow artifacts and 0 releases/tags on the repository. The package is in practice built and delivered manually on the lab, so a reviewer looking for the artifact in Actions or Releases finds nothing and the stated publication guarantee is unbacked. ## Executive Summary

The committed CI is small and genuinely hardened: three workflows, all actions pinned by commit SHA, all downloaded tools SHA-256-verified before execution, hash-pinned Python dependencies, gitleaks tree + full-history scans, actionlint, ruff, shellcheck and zizmor, and one `validate` job that runs 21 repository checks and 50 shell suites. The gate demonstrably works and fails closed (the publication-equality failure at 584e1a3 is a real example), and the f5cb7c9 publication rebind closed the CI-P2-004 regression. The CI-P2-004 fix is verified by run 38110410254 (all steps green).

The current risks are unchanged from 2026-10-09 plus two new documentation/implementation gaps. Runner topology remains the top CI risk: same-repo PRs (including workflow-editing Dependabot PRs) execute on the sudo-capable `edge-builder` runner before review (CI-P1-001, owner-accepted). The auto-merge workflow still holds write scopes with a TOCTOU window and no environment protection (CI-P2-001). The external-smoke monitoring gate still passes on an owner-IP bypass while its artifact claims Access enforcement (CI-P2-002). Repository Actions defaults remain permissive (CI-P2-003). Scheduled/queued runs can be silently starved or dead (CI-P3-001: three 24-hour queue cancellations, no notification wiring), stale probe workflows remain registered (CI-P3-002), the CI incident playbook section 8 still describes pre-fix tool pinning (CI-P3-003), and the review package is documented as a CI/release artifact although no CI job builds or publishes it (CI-P3-004).

Immediate actions: fix the auto-merge head-commit pin (small, high-value), fix or rescope external-smoke, and set read-only Actions defaults. Owner-gated: runner hardening for CI-P1-001.
